Obviously, you can trade, but the tiny cargo space you have leaves a lot to be desired.

The easiest way to make money when you first start is slapping a Kill Warrant Scanner (though it's not required at all) and bounty hunting at the local Nav Beacon.

To find the Nav Beacon, you need to get 'close' to the star in the system you're in, go to your navigation tab, and set it as your destination.

For a little explanation, the nav Beacon in each system acts as a catch all for NPC ships entering the area.

It's mostly filled with other NPC bounty hunters and system security vessels. However, if you hang out there long enough and target every ship that enters, your auto scan will eventually find a ship (or wings of ships) that are wanted. You'll see this when the scan is complete on the target display info.

When you find a wanted pilot, they are fair game to engage, meaning you won't be fined for attacking them.

Once they're dead, you'll get a notification in your transactions tab telling you how much bounty payout you have.

To redeem it, you have to fly to a station that corresponds to the faction or government listed on the transaction.

A few tips :

  1. When starting, it helps if you follow system security vessels around. They will scan all ships also and start attacking locally wanted pilots. The extra firepower will make those early bounty come quicker.

  2. Only attack when the target indicator displays "Wanted". Attacking before the scan finishes will put a bounty on your head, even if the scan shows they are wanted afterwards.

  3. Early on, redeem your bounty vouchers often. If your ship is destroyed, all unredeemed vouchers will be wiped clean. It may not seem like much at first, but it's a good habit to be mindful of it. I personally almost lost 8 million credits the other night at the end of a bounty hunting run when I tried to play chicken with a much better equipped ship than mine.
